title: Partial spontaneous regression of choroidal melanoma: A case image with histopathology and gene expression profiling
content: 1IntroductionSpontaneous regression of cancer is defined as the complete or partial disappearance of a tumor in the absence of treatment. While this phenomenon has been well-documented for cutaneous melanoma, it is quite rare for choroidal melanoma.2Case reportA 74-year-old man presented with vitreous hemorrhage and hand motions visual acuity in the right eye. An elevated amelanotic choroidal lesion was visible in the inferior periphery with associated exudative retinal detachment (Fig. 1a). B-scan demonstrated a choroidal lesion measuring 9.0 mm in thickness and 12.4 × 15.3 mm in basal diameter (9.0 × 12.4 × 15.3 mm) (Fig. 1b). The patient was referred to oncology to investigate potential source of metastasis. PET/CT was negative. Four weeks later, ultrasound revealed a dramatic reduction in size of the mass (3.7 × 10.0 × 11.3 mm) (Fig. 1c and d). Given the significant regression of the lesion, the patient declined further workup and elected observation. Four months after presentation, the lesion had further decreased in size (3.2 × 7.2 × 10.5 mm) and vitreous hemorrhage had resolved (Fig. 1e and f).Fig. 1On presentation, photo of elevated choroidal lesion with vitreous hemorrhage (a) and ultrasound showing dome-shaped lesion with medium internal reflectivity and associated serous retinal detachment (b). Imaging sequences demonstrating regression at four weeks (c–d) and four months (e–f) after presentation. One year later, subsequent increase in tumor dimensions and height (g–h).Fig. 1Upon one-year follow-up, the lesion had increased considerably in size (6.4 × 12.8 × 14.3 mm) (Fig. 1g–h) and a biopsy of the lesion was obtained. Biopsy of the mass confirmed malignant melanoma (Fig. 2a–d). Gene expression profiling revealed a Class IB, PRAME-positive tumor with mutations in GNA11 and SF3B1, suggesting low-intermediate metastatic risk. The patient underwent plaque brachytherapy and transpupillary thermotherapy, resulting in tumor regression without evidence of metastases two years after treatment.Fig. 2Light microscopy at 400 × (a) and 1000 × (b) showing atypical spindle cells. Immunohistochemistry showing pan melanoma (c) and SOX-10 positivity (d).Fig. 23DiscussionThe exact mechanism of spontaneous regression is unknown; it has been linked to hyperactivation of cell-mediated immunity, hormonal influences, necrosis, and vascular insufficiency.1 To our knowledge, only eight cases have been reported, only two of which have documented histological confirmation of melanoma.2,3 There do not appear to be clear patterns for predicting spontaneous regression, though three of the cases were associated with ocular pain and inflammation.3 Here we provide imaging of spontaneous regression with histologic confirmation and gene expression profiling. These gene expression profiling results suggest low metastatic risk for this patient.4ConclusionSpontaneous regression may rarely be observed with choroidal melanoma, which may inadvertently delay treatment. Close surveillance and a high index of suspicion are essential for diagnosis in these patients.Patient consentVerbal informed consent was obtained from the patient.FundingThe author(s) received no financial support for the research, authorship, and/or publication of this article.AuthorshipAll authors attest that they meet the current ICMJE criteria for Authorship.Declaration of competing interestThe authors declare the following financial interests/personal relationships which may be considered as potential competing interests: Dan S. diagnosis.diagnosis_raw: Elevated amelanotic choroidal lesion; later biopsy confirmed malignant melanoma (choroidal melanoma).
diagnosis.disease_name: Choroidal melanoma (malignant melanoma of the choroid), amelanotic
diagnosis.severity_description: Ocular tumor with exudative retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage; later gene expression profiling Class IB, PRAME-positive; low-intermediate metastatic risk.
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Vitreous hemorrhage with hand motions visual acuity in the right eye; associated exudative retinal detachment.
diagnosis.cancer_subtype: Choroidal melanoma (amelanotic); spindle cell morphology noted on microscopy
diagnosis.histology: malignant melanoma with atypical spindle cells; immunohistochemistry positive for pan melanoma and SOX-10

treatment.treatments_raw: After biopsy confirmation at one-year follow-up, patient underwent plaque brachytherapy and transpupillary thermotherapy.

remission_outcome.time_to_remission_raw: Dramatic reduction in tumor size at 4 weeks after presentation; further decrease by 4 months.
remission_outcome.verification_detail: Initial tumor measured 9.0 mm thickness and 12.4 × 15.3 mm basal diameter on B-scan; PET/CT negative for metastasis; at 4 weeks ultrasound showed 3.7 × 10.0 × 11.3 mm; at 4 months 3.2 × 7.2 × 10.5 mm. At 1 year tumor increased to 6.4 × 12.8 × 14.3 mm; biopsy confirmed melanoma. After plaque brachytherapy + transpupillary thermotherapy, tumor regressed with no metastases at 2 years.
remission_outcome.tumor_response: Partial spontaneous regression followed by later progression; subsequent post-treatment regression.
remission_outcome.tumor_size_change: 9.0 × 12.4 × 15.3 mm to 3.7 × 10.0 × 11.3 mm at 4 weeks; to 3.2 × 7.2 × 10.5 mm at 4 months; then increased to 6.4 × 12.8 × 14.3 mm at 1 year.
remission_outcome.follow_up_duration_raw: No evidence of metastases two years after treatment.
remission_outcome.recurrence_timing: One year after presentation the lesion increased considerably in size.

agency_examples: Declined further workup after early regression and elected observation
turner_factors.agency_details: After significant early regression, the patient declined further workup and chose observation.

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Spontaneous regression is described as rare for choroidal melanoma; only a small number of cases reported in the literature per discussion.
validation.extraction_notes: Organ system classified as integumentary because melanoma is a skin-lineage cancer, though primary site is ocular choroid; staging not provided. Early regression was imaging-based before biopsy confirmation (biopsy occurred after later regrowth).

analysis.case_summary: A 74-year-old man presented with a right-eye amelanotic choroidal lesion that showed marked size reduction on ultrasound over 4 weeks and further regression by 4 months without treatment, followed by regrowth at 1 year when biopsy confirmed malignant melanoma. He then received plaque brachytherapy and transpupillary thermotherapy with subsequent regression and no metastases reported two years later.
key_healing_factors: Imaging-documented partial spontaneous regression of the choroidal mass prior to any ocular tumor-directed therapy
No metastatic disease detected on PET/CT at initial workup
Subsequent definitive local therapy (plaque brachytherapy and transpupillary thermotherapy) leading to regression
unique_features: Rare partial spontaneous regression in choroidal melanoma documented with serial imaging
Histopathologic confirmation and gene expression profiling (Class IB, PRAME-positive; GNA11 and SF3B1 mutations) obtained after later tumor regrowth
analysis.analysis_notes: The spontaneous regression phase occurred before histologic confirmation; melanoma diagnosis was confirmed only after subsequent enlargement at one year. No psycho-spiritual factors were described in the narrative.
